topic.label: Research
topic.desc: Research as a working discipline: framing questions, finding and appraising literature, designing and analysing studies, replication, synthesis, writing and integrity. Extends the base Research topic, which held only Latent Space.

concepts: Turning a topic into answerable questions, hypotheses, scope limits and success criteria before any searching starts.
Searching, screening and tracking papers: search strings, citation chasing, screening rules and annotated bibliographies.
Judging how far a source can be trusted: study design, bias, peer review versus preprint, conflicts of interest and retraction status.
Designing studies and experiments: controls, sampling, sample size, preregistration and what would count as a negative result.
Analysing results and checking whether they hold: statistics, robustness checks, reproducible pipelines and replication attempts.
Combining many sources into one picture: evidence tables, agreement and conflict between studies, stated confidence and open gaps.
Writing papers and reports: structure, claims tied to evidence, related work, abstracts, figures and correct citation.
Keeping research honest and lawful: provenance, data licences, consent, authorship, disclosure of tool and AI use, and conflicts of interest.
skills: Turns a vague topic into a few answerable questions with a hypothesis for each and a statement of what would change the conclusion.
Writes inclusion and exclusion criteria, time window and success measures so the work can be judged finished.
Lists what is already known, what is assumed and what is disputed on a topic so new work does not repeat settled ground.
Builds search strings with synonyms and filters for several databases and records exactly what was run and when.
Screens titles and abstracts against the written criteria and logs every inclusion and exclusion with its reason.
Follows references forwards and backwards from key papers to find work the keyword search missed, and lists what each hop added.
Summarises each source in a few lines with its method, finding and limit, kept in one shareable list.
Classifies a study as trial, cohort, case study, simulation or opinion and says what that design can and cannot show.
Looks for selection bias, confounding, p-hacking and selective reporting and states how each would change the result.
Checks whether a paper is peer reviewed, revised, corrected or retracted and reports the date and source of that status.
Writes a plan with variables, controls, procedure and the measurements that will be taken, before any data exists.
Estimates the sample needed to detect an effect of a stated size and shows the assumptions behind the number.
Drafts a timestamped plan of hypotheses and analyses so later choices cannot quietly change the question.
Runs the planned tests, reports effect sizes with intervals rather than only p-values, and lists every test that was tried.
Re-runs an analysis with other reasonable choices of data cleaning, model and threshold and reports whether the finding survives.
Packages data, code, versions and random seeds so another person can regenerate every table and figure.
Plans a direct or conceptual replication of a published result and says what outcome would count as failing to replicate.
Builds a table of studies by population, method, measure and result so agreement and conflict are visible side by side.
Rates how strongly the evidence supports each claim and writes the reason for the grade next to it.
Lists questions the literature leaves open or answers only weakly, ranked by how much an answer would change decisions.
Lays out a paper with one claim per section and the evidence each section must cite.
Writes a related-work section that groups sources by idea, states how this work differs and cites each source correctly.
Formats references in a named style, checks each against its source record and flags entries that cannot be found.
Records where every dataset, figure and quotation came from, under what licence and on what date it was retrieved.
Tool and AI Use Disclosure Writer
Writes a plain statement of which tools and AI systems helped with which step and what a person checked afterwards.
Checks that consent, ethics review, data licences and conflicts of interest are documented before data is used or published.
Estimates the time, data access, skills and cost a question needs and says whether to narrow it before work starts.
Reads funding statements and author disclosures and says which findings could be shaped by who paid for the work.
Writes the step-by-step protocol, form fields and quality checks for gathering data so different collectors get comparable results.
Plans the pooling of comparable studies: effect measure, heterogeneity checks, fixed versus random effects and sensitivity analyses.
Answers each reviewer comment point by point, says what changed in the manuscript and politely explains what did not.
Writes where research data will be stored, who may access it, how long it is kept and how sensitive records are protected.
